claims.claim: Expectancy- and placebo-related mechanisms can produce measurable subjective and physiological responses.
claims.correction: Say "can produce measurable changes in pain reports and, in experimental placebo-analgesia research, neural and some peripheral physiological measures"; do not imply broad disease modification across conditions.

citations.author: Zunhammer et al.
citations.finding_supported: Participant-level meta-analysis of 20 fMRI placebo-analgesia studies (603 healthy participants) found reproducible placebo-related alterations in brain systems, while also reporting substantial heterogeneity.

citations.author: Hróbjartsson and Gøtzsche
citations.finding_supported: Systematic review of placebo-versus-no-treatment trials found possible beneficial effects particularly for patient-reported outcomes such as pain, but no large general clinical effect.

claims.claim: Open-label placebo has been studied as an add-on treatment approach for chronic low back pain.
claims.correction: Name the study and characterize it as a short randomized trial of open-label placebo plus treatment as usual versus treatment as usual—not proof that it treats underlying back pathology.

citations.author: Carvalho, Caetano, Cunha, Rebouta, Kaptchuk, and Kirsch
citations.finding_supported: Randomized 97 adults with persistent low back pain; 83 completed three weeks. Open-label placebo plus treatment as usual had greater reductions in self-reported composite pain (1.5 versus 0.2 points) and disability (2.9 versus 0.0 points) than treatment as usual.

claims.claim: Some open-label placebo effects may occur without deception or a conventional belief that the pill contains active medicine.
claims.correction: Replace "belief is irrelevant" with "deception and belief that the pill contains an active drug are not necessary in some studies; a credible rationale, positive expectations, conditioning, context, and adherence may still matter."

citations.author: Kaptchuk et al.
citations.finding_supported: In an IBS randomized trial, participants were explicitly told that pills were placebo; the open-label-placebo group improved more than a no-treatment control on reported global improvement and symptom severity.

citations.author: Buergler et al.
citations.finding_supported: Network meta-analysis treated at least minimal positive expectation induced alongside administration as an inclusion feature and examined expectation, comparator, route, and population as effect modifiers.

citations.author: Colloca et al.
citations.finding_supported: Experimental work found that learning/conditioning potentiated behavioral and neurophysiological placebo-analgesic responses.

claims.claim: Copables is a company that mails inert pills to customers.
claims.correction: The defensible version is: "Copables' own website describes a protocol involving a physical placebo and a handwritten daily card." Do not state that it mails pills, what the pills contain, or that they are inert until product, ingredients, fulfillment, and terms are independently verified.

citations.author: Copables
citations.finding_supported: Company self-description says its protocol includes "your placebo" and a daily handwritten card; it presents open-label-placebo research as its scientific basis. This is not independent confirmation of its product contents or delivery model.

claims.claim: A digital intervention might reproduce some therapeutic components of a placebo ritual without a physical pill.
claims.correction: Call this a testable design hypothesis: a phone can deliver instructions, timing, reminders, feedback, and expectancy cues, but equivalence to a physical open-label placebo ritual has not been established.

citations.author: Stalujanis et al.
citations.finding_supported: A 132-participant randomized study used a 20-day smartphone-based digital placebo intervention to manipulate and measure credibility and efficacy expectancies; it studied expectancies, not clinical equivalence to placebo pills.

citations.author: Buergler et al.
citations.finding_supported: Administration route is a studied potential modifier of open-label placebo effects, which weighs against assuming that a phone and pill are interchangeable.

claims.claim: Ted Kaptchuk is associated with the Program in Placebo Studies & Therapeutic Encounter at BIDMC and Harvard Medical School.
claims.correction: Use the current institutional wording: "Ted J. Kaptchuk is Professor Emeritus at Harvard Medical School and a member of the research faculty at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center; BIDMC lists the Program in Placebo Studies & Therapeutic Encounter."

citations.author: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center
citations.finding_supported: Current BIDMC profile identifies Kaptchuk as Professor Emeritus at Harvard Medical School, BIDMC research faculty, and links the Program in Placebo Studies & Therapeutic Encounter.

strongest_evidence.why: Direct randomized clinical evidence for the chronic-low-back-pain assertion, with sample, comparator, duration, and outcome estimates.
Foundational primary trial showing an open-label placebo protocol can outperform no treatment for IBS symptom outcomes.
Large individual-participant fMRI meta-analysis supporting measurable neurobiological correlates in experimental placebo analgesia.
Necessary limiting evidence: subjective effects, especially pain, should not be inflated into a general claim of major clinical efficacy.

counterevidence.finding: The placebo-versus-no-treatment evidence base does not support a sweeping claim of clinically important benefit across conditions; effects are more evident for subjective continuous outcomes such as pain.
Open-label placebo research commonly uses an explanatory rationale and positive framing; evidence does not establish that expectation, credibility, or context are irrelevant.
The cited smartphone study measured induced expectancies, not symptom relief or equivalence with a pill-based open-label placebo.

open_questions.question: Did the Carvalho trial measure expectancy, credibility, adherence, or objective physical-function outcomes sufficiently to identify mechanism?
What exactly does Copables sell; are its pills pharmacologically inert; what are the ingredients; and are products physically mailed to customers?
Are Copables' efficacy statements descriptions of published research or claims tested on the company's own protocol?
Can a digital-only open-label ritual match pill-based outcomes in the same condition, with comparable rationale, contact, adherence, and outcome assessment?

sources_to_verify.needed: Official product, ingredient, fulfillment, terms, privacy, and purchase pages; independent confirmation of the product description.
Full Carvalho methods/results tables for pill instructions, adherence, expectancy measurement, and objective-versus-self-reported outcomes.
Program landing page or institutional directory confirming the program's current formal name and leadership.
